In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ovulatory response of estrogen-primed rabbits to intraventriculat NE is mediated by a noradrenergically sensitive histaminergic pathway which is probably located in the midbrain.

histamine is a central neurotransmitter, that it activates the hypothalamo-hypophyseal system and that the activation of the system by histamine is due to the stimulation of central noradrengic elements.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the olfactory bulb is a major site for the central control of pituitary- ovarian function, but that the bulb is not the only such site.
histamine is a central nervous activator and NE is a central nervous transmitter.
the central nervous system is a major regulator of pituitary- gonadal function and that the hypothalamus and olfactory bulb are the most important brain regions involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the olfactory bulb is a major site of action of NE in the induction of ovulation.
the olfactory bulb and its central projections are important for the central activation of the ovulatory process.

we need to think about the role of the olfactory system in reproductive behavior, and we need to think of it not just in the context of pheromones, but also in the context of the olfactory bulbs being a site of action for a number of different neuroactive compounds.
